holidays.name: National Cheese Toast Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble, gooey glory of bread topped with melted cheese. Whether it's a fancy gruyère on sourdough or a slice of American under the broiler, today is your excuse to get melty.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it emerged from the unofficial food-holiday calendar and is promoted by food enthusiasts and social media rather than an act of Congress. Its exact founder is unknown.
holidays.funFact: Melted cheese on bread has ancient roots: Welsh rarebit, a cousin of cheese toast, was being served in Britain by the 1700s, and its name was probably a joke implying that poor Welsh folk couldn't afford actual rabbit.

holidays.name: National Online Learning Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to appreciating the ability to learn anything from quantum physics to sourdough baking, all in your pajamas. It celebrates the courses, tutorials, and videos that have turned the internet into a giant classroom.
holidays.origin: It was established in the 2010s to recognize the growth of e-learning and digital education, and it gained a lot of attention as remote learning became widespread.
holidays.funFact: Distance education is much older than the internet: in 1728, a Boston newspaper ad offered to mail weekly shorthand lessons to students.

holidays.name: International Day of Democracy
holidays.description: A day for celebrating and reflecting on democratic principles, civic participation, and the idea that everyone gets a say, even in arguments about pineapple on pizza.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly established it in 2007, encouraging governments and citizens to promote and uphold democratic values.
holidays.funFact: The word democracy comes from the Greek words demos (people) and kratos (power), and in ancient Athens some officials were chosen by lottery rather than elections.

holidays.name: Felt Hat Day
holidays.description: The unofficial opposite of the old rule that you must stop wearing white after Labor Day: today marks the traditional time to swap out straw hats for felt ones. Fedoras and fancy toppers are ready for their closeup.
holidays.origin: This is rooted in early 20th-century American fashion etiquette, when men switched from straw boaters to felt hats on or around September 15. The date was observed so seriously that some men reportedly had their straw hats smashed if they were seen wearing them after the deadline.
holidays.funFact: In 1922, the unofficial Straw Hat Day deadline led to the so-called 'Straw Hat Riots' in New York City, where gangs of young men and boys knocked hats off people's heads and stomped on them.

holidays.name: National Double Cheeseburger Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate stacking twice the patties and twice the cheese on a bun. Because one patty is for ordinary days, and today is for extra deliciousness.
holidays.origin: This burger-themed observance is a product of the American food-holiday calendar, popular with restaurant chains that offer deals on double burgers on this date.
holidays.funFact: The cheeseburger is said to have been invented in the 1920s or 1930s, and a number of restaurants in different states each claim to have been first to put cheese on a patty.
